searchText: What is the state of the art for staking security? Is it just "put your private keys on a host and hope that the host is never compromised"? And if the host is compromised, what is the max loss in such a scenario? secret-shared validators are helpful What is the 10,000 foot description of that? Slightly longer than "secret-shared validators". 😄 https://unvetica.com/eth-staker-community-call-10-secret-shared-validators-and-trustless-staking-pools/ and a proof of concept: https://github.com/dankrad/python-ssv I'm not in a position to listen to audio right now. Is there a text description somewhere? Ah, readme of the second link was enough. Split your key and deploy it across multiple machines then sign with the majority of machines. Better than having the key on a single machine, though I still worry about the OpSec required. What is the worst case loss if my validator signing key is compromised? Griefing, blackmail, or forging a slashing that can then be mined by attacker for a small gain But full signing key has to be leaked first ofc. A SSV should make this difficult Assuming the attacker's goal is to cause me as much financial harm as possible, what can they do? Can they wipe me out? Cause me to lose 1%? Cause me to gain nothing and lose nothing? It depends on context how severe slashings are. If you're the only one in a long time period, it will be light. The opposite can also happen Hmm, I guess I'll need to read more in depth. As a potential validator, a document that focuses on explaining the risks would be valuable. Something that doesn't require I go and fully understand validation, but instead gives me only the information I need to do a risk assessment. The max an attacker can do is get you slashed, which is ~1ETH under normal circumstances but can be up to 100% of your balance if the attacker gets a large number of other validators slashed at the same time That would be a very difficult attack to pull off, however Also for the first few months of mainnet slashing penalties have been reduced from that baseline
